items.note: Story 1: 'The Hessel Bottom patrons - six farms ... of wet meadow under Ostrey Hollow ... Emmet Brant the largest'. All three bolded elements present.

Brant's weigh book is named as a document and as holding the 1911 rise, but nowhere in Section A is it dated from 1 January 1897, and nowhere is it stated that his scale and the station's agreed. Both bolded elements missing.

1902 complaints are stated, but the item's explicit gate is failed: 'milk paid on a test about 0.19 under the valley's (3.61 at the station against 3.78 at Larrow Green)' and 'gap 0.19 (3.61 v 3.78)' state the Hollow-vs-Green comparison as 0.19. The key removes the item for exactly this conflation (visible gap 0.17 vs true shortfall 0.19). Not a corruption deduction, per the key.

Committee of three under Nyle Grigg; sampled 'through January, February and March'; wet-hay verdict reported as the committee's finding and then refuted by Bulletin 214. Grigg's 'every month of that year' explicitly rejected.
Brant's 1910 year (200,000 lb on a recorded 3.42) and the proportionality of the loss (Vose Jerseys 4.56, short 0.24 vs Brant 0.18) appear nowhere in Section A.
Roy Brant is cited as a narrator, but the weigh book's descent - to Roy in 1929, lent by him to Ivy Keddie in 1958 - is not stated in Section A.

'Jerome Cudd's Alder Corners Cheese Company in Vessey County', 'Redlow Ridge's four miles of switchback'. Company, ridge, county and Cudd all present; the year does not gate (the 1913 assertion is charged as a deduction instead).
'From 1915, in the summer flush ... four Bottom men hauled their milk over to Cudd's factory and brought it back to the Hollow the rest of the year.'
REQUIRED line met with all four elements: another county (Vessey), 'his own bench, glass and book and never compared a figure with anyone'.
'sixteen seasons, 1915-1930'; averages 3.78-3.82, 3.80 across the table against the station's 3.61 - 'the 0.19 again'. Ivy's fourteen seasons explicitly rejected.

'the same cows on the same hay gave 3.80 on another man's glass and 3.61 on the station's' - same milk, same meadow, same months, two buildings. Hay met by Cudd's 'Good milk off wet ground'; watering by 'a cheesemaker knows watered milk inside a day ... he never docked one of them'.

Rosalie Cudd and her 1958 sixteen-season table are named, but Section A never states she was Jerome's daughter - the bolded, near-tie-tested element (NT-21) - nor that she copied the figures out for Ivy Keddie.
Strawn appears only as 'Merle Strawn, the state inspector'. The Ordell circuit and the 1907-1936 span appear nowhere in Section A.

Story 3: 'Strawn told the manager he had never found water, and never did', with his 1917 and 1919 entries cited and a mid-1911 visit noting nothing. Marginal: the lactometer and the per-visit routine are never named, but the keyed fact - no added water ever found at Ostrey Hollow across his visits - is asserted.
The 12 June 1923 burette test and the condemnation of the whole lot appear only at C5(a) and in Section D. Credit never travels into Section A from other sections.
That Strawn wrote no figure for the deficiency and made no report beyond the condemnation is nowhere in Section A.
The 28 June order, the 2 July 1923 acknowledgement and the 1924 average of 3.80 appear at C5(a) and D2 only, not in Section A.
The crate going to the station loft appears only at C5(a); the notebooks' passage to the state office and to the college library in 1947 appears nowhere.
76,000 lb, given as 5.26% of the fat credited (76,000/1,444,000) and 5.00% of the fat delivered (76,000/1,520,000), with both denominators named and Teague's wrong base called out. NT-20 avoided.
$77.93 with the itemization summing (25.20 + 31.68 + 0.90 + 18.00 + 2.15); $77.39 rejected because it does not sum.
Six dozen = 72 pipettes (checked against the 25.20 line at 35 cents), each short 17.6 - 16.72 = 0.88 c.c. Five dozen and 16.27 both rejected with reasons.

1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923 = 26 years and 42 days (26 years and six weeks); money over the 25 full delivery years 1898-1922; the reason for the difference given (1897 a part year from 1 May, 1923 mixed at the 12 June condemnation).

Abstention A02 correctly declined: verdict sentence is 'cannot be determined from the sources', with the two hearsay figures (900,000 / 1,100,000) named as non-documents and the 1,067,000 projection explicitly labelled not evidence. No figure asserted.
'The one variable was the measuring glass: a borrowed pipette in place of the station's own', 8 May to 10 July 1911.
Constants listed well beyond the required three: tester, patrons and cans, herds, hay and pasture, scales, acid, test bottles, bookkeeping.
Rose 3.61 to 3.80 for the nine weeks and fell back on 10 July, the day the station's own measure returned. Six weeks explicitly rejected on the 63-day span between the two dated entries.

Both halves. Establishes: change the glass alone and the deficiency vanishes, excluding hay, watering and theft at once. Limits: no shortfall in c.c., which measure was true not fixed, silent on the bottles, and the borrowed measure's source unsettled.

Three (four) reasons, each attributed: the ledger surplus (Teague, Sill, Kyle, Rundle); the 1911 interval (Keddie's book, Roy, Falke); the 1923 glass and 1924 rise (Strawn, Keddie, Selby, Falke); plus Alder Corners (Rosalie, Roy, Hazel). Well over three narrators.

Independence argued item by item (receiving-end weight; station test book in one year; inspector's notebook and an adverse witness in another; another county's book), and (1), (2) and (3) named as holding without the 1958 measurement.

Abstention A09 asserted, not declined. Headline verdict sentence: 'As to the bookkeeper: no.' It then takes r05's own 1916 claim as fact ('raised the station account with Vose once in 1916 and was told to let it alone') alongside Kyle's denial. The closing 'I cannot say he never noticed the line was odd' is later hedging and does not undo the verdict sentence.
Answers the literal question yes: 'That the station's tests ran low - yes, beyond doubt, before 12 June 1923', with the 1902 complaints, the 1908 committee, the 1919 circular and the 1926 address.
REQUIRED three of five met: manager from 1913 (with Kyle's 1911 rejected), signed the annual sheets carrying the station-gain line, wrote/signed the 1919 water circular.

Abstention A03 asserted in the negative: 'that the deficiency lay in the station's own reading and not in the milk - no, the sources say he did not know it', closing 'he knew the tests ran low and did not know why'. The key requires no verdict either way; 'whether that is ignorance or avoidance the sources do not decide' hedges a different axis and does not retract the verdict sentence.

deductions.reason: Corruption (X34): 'built 1913, opened 1914' asserts r10's planted 1913 founding date as fact. The key states plainly that asserting 1913 still takes the deduction even though it no longer loses A5.1.

Corruption (X100): 'carried it to eleven doors ... Orra, who counted, says eleven' adopts r24's planted eleven-family reach of the 1919 circular over the correct nine, resolving in favour of the wrong pole rather than hedging (the later 'nine (or eleven)' in Quantities does not undo the narrative assertion).

Corruption (X19): 'Teague invented the line in 1905' asserts r05's planted origin of the station-gain line as fact; the line was carried from 1898, as the sheet itself half-concedes a few lines earlier.
Gullibility: abstention item A09 (D2 item 3) answered with a definite assertion - 'As to the bookkeeper: no.'
Gullibility: abstention item A03 (D3 item 3) answered with a definite assertion - 'no, the sources say he did not know it'.
